CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
In RAN1#107-e, following coclusion was reached:
Conclusion
For two linked SS sets are configured with respective searchSpaceGroupIdList, 
If both SS sets are monitored in a search space set group, then PDCCH repetition mechanism is applied for the linked SS sets
If only one of the two SS sets is monitored in a search space set group, then the legacy PDCCH mechanism is applied for the monitored one (i.e., no PDCCH repetition)

According to above conclusion, when the PDCCH repetition is indicated by higher layer parameter searchspaceLinkingID, the PDCCH repetition mechanism should be applied only when both SS sets are monitored in a search space set group. However, the exting description in 38.213 implies that PDCCH repetition mecahnisms are always applied even when only one of the two SS sets is monitored in a search space set group, which is not consistent with the conclusion above.

CR_anchor.properties_json: {"consequencesIfNotApproved":"UE would apply the wrong set of power control parameters to PUSCH transmission to a TRP associated to the second SRS resource set","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"344.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208067","reasonForChange":"When two SRS resource sets are configured for  DCI format 0_1 or DCI format 0_2 and if a SRS resource set indicator indicating one of the SRS resource sets  is present  in a DCI, but an corresponding SRI field is not present in the DCI, a default power control parameter is supposed to be used and if the open-loop power control parameter set indication  field  is not included in the DCI, the the default parameters are specified by the the first and second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets for the first and second SRS resource sets, respectively. \n\nHowever, in the current specification, it is stated that the first P0-PUSCH-AlphaSet in p0-AlphaSets is used as the default power control parameters  when either one of the two SRS resource sets is indicated, which is incorrect.","reservationDate":"8/25/2022 6:28:57 AM","status":"agreed","summaryOfChange":"A change is made to state that when the second SRS resource set is indicated in the DCI, parameters in the second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets are used  for PUSCH power control.","tdocNumber":"R1-2208067","title":"CR on default PUSCH power control parameters for mTRP PUSCH","tsgCRPack":"RP-222400","type":"CR","uploadedDate":"2022-08-28T18:21:16.693000"}
CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
When two SRS resource sets are configured for  DCI format 0_1 or DCI format 0_2 and if a SRS resource set indicator indicating one of the SRS resource sets  is present  in a DCI, but an corresponding SRI field is not present in the DCI, a default power control parameter is supposed to be used and if the open-loop power control parameter set indication  field  is not included in the DCI, the the default parameters are specified by the the first and second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets for the first and second SRS resource sets, respectively. 

However, in the current specification, it is stated that the first P0-PUSCH-AlphaSet in p0-AlphaSets is used as the default power control parameters  when either one of the two SRS resource sets is indicated, which is incorrect.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: A change is made to state that when the second SRS resource set is indicated in the DCI, parameters in the second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets are used  for PUSCH power control.
CR_anchor.title: CR on default PUSCH power control parameters for mTRP PUSCH

When the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11, two SRS resource sets are associated with different PUSCHs, and two sets of power control parameters would be determined according to 38.213. However, the association between the two sets of power control parameters and the two SRS resource sets is absent in 38.213. It is unclear whether the first and second set of power control parameters (e.g. ) are associated with the first and second set of SRS resource set, or associated with the first and second PUSCH repetition respectively. They are different cases when the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11. CR_anchor.reasonForChange: If a UE is provided two SRS resource sets for PUSCH repetition by RRC, one or two SRI(s)/SRS resource set(s) can be indicated for PUSCH transmission via SRS resource set indicator in DCI. When the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11, two SRS resource sets are associated with different PUSCHs, and two sets of power control parameters would be determined according to 38.213. However, the association between the two sets of power control parameters and the two SRS resource sets is absent in 38.213. It is unclear whether the first and second set of power control parameters (e.g. ) are associated with the first and second set of SRS resource set, or associated with the first and second PUSCH repetition respectively. They are different cases when the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11. When the SRS resource set indicator value is 00 and 01, only one SRS resource set is associated with PUSCH and only one set of power control parameters is determined based on 38.213, and there is no ambiguity for the mapping.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: The first set of power control parameters is associated with the first SRS resource set, and the second set of power control parameters is associated with the second SRS resource set.

CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
In 38.214, SSBs associated with additional PCIs are not considered as invalid symbols for PUSCH repetition Type B. 
Avoiding such conflict by network implementation may not be practical since scheduling PUSCH repetition type B by any TRP may have to be delayed until after any SSB associated with any additional PCI, which is against the motivation of PUSCH repetition Type B for latency reduction.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: In 38.214, add SSBs indicated by ssb-PositionsInBurst in SSB-MTCAdditionalPCI as invalid symbols for PUSCH repetition Type B.
CR_anchor.title: CR on inter-cell mTRP with PUSCH repetition TypeB

CR_anchor.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE behavior will remain undefined when SSBs that the UE measures for L1-RSRP/SINR (and are not associated with the PCI that has active TCI states) overlap with UL channels/signals.
CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
For inter-cell mTRP in FeMIMO, the following has been agreed in RAN1#108-e:


In 38.213, the “active additional PCI” in the agreement is captured as the PCI associated with the active TCI states. However, this is problematic as UE still measures SSBs (L1 measurment) from the PCIs not associated with the active TCI states.
When SSBs that the UE measures for L1-RSRP/SINR (and are not associated with the PCI that has active TCI states) overlap with UL channels/signals, there is no procedure currently defined as to whether the UE should measure the SSB or transmit the UL channel/signal given that the UE is not capable of full-duplex operation in TDD.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: Remove the condition “associated to physical cell ID with active TCI states” in relevant sections.
CR_anchor.title: CR on inter-cell mTRP when SSBs of additional PCI overlap with UL

CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
In RAN1#109-e, following was agreed. However, TP was not discussed, due to the lack of time. Hence, we propose TP to capture the agreement.
Agreement
If scheduling offset < threshold (timeDurationForQCL ), regardless of configuration of followUnifiedTCIstate 
If the indicated TCI is associated with PCI different from serving cell PCI  (i.e. inter-cell),
UE should apply Rel.15 default QCL assumption for both non-UE dedicated and UE dedicated PDSCH (i.e. QCL assumption of the lowest CORESET ID in the latest slot)
If the QCL -TypeD property for default beams in a slot for CCs in a band are different, the default beam for the CC with lowest ID is prioritized, i.e. the default beam for the CC with lowest ID is applied to all the CCs in a band
If the indicated TCI  is associated with serving cell PCI  (i.e. intra-cell), UE  always uses indicated TCI  for both UE -dedicated/non-UE -dedicated PDSCH  (i.e. no need to consider default QCL ) 
The same approach above is applied to default beam for aperiodic CSI -RS
Note: UE is not expected to receive a non-UE dedicated PDSCH if the source RS of the TCI state of the corresponding PDSCH is not associated with the serving cell PCID . 
Note: when the above was agreed on email, last two sub-bullets were two “bullets”, which are applied to all the agreement. However, in final chairman’s note, these two bullets are incorrectly noted as sub-bullets.

CR_anchor.consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear whether the TCI update signaling is applied to all configured BWP(s) or active BWP, and whether the BAT should count the BeamAppTime_r17 in all configured BWP(s) or in active BWP only.
CR_anchor.properties_json: {"consequencesIfNotApproved":"It is unclear whether the TCI update signaling is applied to all configured BWP(s) or active BWP, and whether the BAT should count the BeamAppTime_r17 in all configured BWP(s) or in active BWP only.","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"316.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208100","reasonForChange":"When the TCI state update signaling is applied to all configured BWPs and the BAT counts BeamAppTime_r17 in all configured BWPs, there is a possibility that the SCS configured for an inactive BWP is smaller than that for the active BWPs in the configured CC list, and is used to determine the beam application time for all configured CCs/BWPs, which leads to unnecessary large latency.","reservationDate":"8/25/2022 8:17:28 AM","status":"agreed","summaryOfChange":"In TS38.214 section 5.1.5, clarify that the TCI update signaling is applied to active BWP, and the BAT should count the BeamAppTime_r17 in active BWP only.","tdocNumber":"R1-2208100","title":"CR on BAT for CA case","tsgCRPack":"RP-222400","type":"CR","uploadedDate":"2022-08-28T18:21:17.007000"}
CR_anchor.reasonForChange: When the TCI state update signaling is applied to all configured BWPs and the BAT counts BeamAppTime_r17 in all configured BWPs, there is a possibility that the SCS configured for an inactive BWP is smaller than that for the active BWPs in the configured CC list, and is used to determine the beam application time for all configured CCs/BWPs, which leads to unnecessary large latency.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: In TS38.214 section 5.1.5, clarify that the TCI update signaling is applied to active BWP, and the BAT should count the BeamAppTime_r17 in active BWP only.
CR_anchor.title: CR on BAT for CA case

CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
In RAN1#109-e UE capability discussion, it was agreed to introduce a new basic feature for MTRP CSI, FG23-7-1c, which indicates the number of CPUs occupied by an NCJT CSI calculation which can be 2, 3 or 4. In the current specification text of Clause 5.2.1.6 in 38.214, the number of CPUs per NCJT CSI is fixed to 2. Moreover, whole paragraph is within brackets which gives rise to ambiguity of supported values.  

Therefore current specification is not aligned with RAN1 agreement made in RAN1 #109-e.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange:
Define the number of CPUs occupied by an MTRP CSI report as “” 
Clarify that the value of parameter X subject to UE capability report.
Remove the brackets from that paragraph.
CR_anchor.title: Correction on the number of CPUs for Multi-TRP CSI

CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
In R15/16, the maximum number of CSI-RS ports contained by each resource per CSI-RS resource set is 16 when Ks=2 and is 8 when 2<Ks≤8. 

For multi-TRP CSI feedback configured for given CSI-RS resource set, the UE complexity to process individual single-TRP resource, e.g. for Mode 2 which will determine multi-TRP or single-TRP CSI to be reported by UE itself, should not be increased beyond R15/16 restrictions.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: Reuse Rel-15/16 CSI-RS port restrictions for each CMR group of CSI-RS resource set, depending on value of max{K1, K2}
CR_anchor.title: Correction on CSI-RS port restriction for mTRP CSI

CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
The brackets for configuring slot offsets of the two resources in a CSI resource pair for Multi-TRP CSI measurement shall be removed in order to capture following agreement and avoid ambiguous understanding of CSI-RS resource configuration at time domain:

For CSI measurement associated with a CSI-ReportingConfig for NCJT, support two CMRs within the same CMR pair configured for NCJT measurement hypothesis to be restricted within X continuous slot(s) without DL/UL switch between two CMRs
X=1, 2
whereas X=1 implying the same slot and X=2 implying two adjacent slots
FFS other restrictions for FR2
FFS whether UE capability is needed for X=2
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: Remove the bracket for slot offsets of two CSI-RS resources within a CSI-RS resource pair.

CR_anchor.reasonForChange:
For Rel-17 NCJT CSI reporting, the UE will report a joint RI index corresponding to one of four RI combinations. The assumption that each CSI report indicates rank 1 in 38.213 for CSI report multiplexing is ambiguous when determining PUCCH payload for Part 2 CSI since the joint RI index (or RI combination) can be interpreted differently, for example considering rank combination {1,2} as rank 1. 
Moreover, for NCJT “Mode 2”, the payload of part 2 CSI is varied depending on the preference of transmission hypothesis reported by the UE, i.e. single TRP CSI or NCJT CSI determined by the value of CRI. It gives rise to further ambiguity of determining hypothetical PUCCH resource assignment or a number of part 2 CSI reports if multiplexing NCJT Mode 2 CSI reports.
CR_anchor.summaryOfChange: It is clarified that for multiplexing CSI reports involving NCJT CSI measurement hypothesis, the UE shall assume rank combination of {1,1}. Also for “Mode 2” selecting the CSI among NCJT and single-TRP preferred by the UE, the UE shall assume NCJT measurement hypothesis used for determining PUCCH resource or the number of CSI reports.
CR_anchor.title: Correction of CSI assumptions over multiplexing NCJT CSI reports in PUCCH

CR_anchor.consequencesIfNotApproved: If a CSI-ReportConfig is configured with groupBasedBeamReporting-r17, other CSI-ReportConfig associated with the trigger state(s) configured using the higher layer parameter CSI-AperiodicTriggerState must be configured with groupBasedBeamReporting-r17; otherwise, no CSI-ReportConfig is configured with groupBasedBeamReporting-r17. Thus the configuration flexibility of beam reporting is meanless.

{"consequencesIfNotApproved":"When PDCCH repetition is configured together with SSSG switching, current specification would be inconsistent with the conclusion.","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"332.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2207945","reasonForChange":"In RAN1#107-e, following coclusion was reached:
Conclusion
For two linked SS sets are configured with respective searchSpaceGroupIdList, 
If both SS sets are monitored in a search space set group, then PDCCH repetition mechanism is applied for the linked SS sets
If only one of the two SS sets is monitored in a search space set group, then the legacy PDCCH mechanism is applied for the monitored one (i.e., no PDCCH repetition)

old_anchors.reasonForChange:
In RAN1#107-e, following coclusion was reached:
Conclusion
For two linked SS sets are configured with respective searchSpaceGroupIdList, 
If both SS sets are monitored in a search space set group, then PDCCH repetition mechanism is applied for the linked SS sets
If only one of the two SS sets is monitored in a search space set group, then the legacy PDCCH mechanism is applied for the monitored one (i.e., no PDCCH repetition)

According to above conclusion, when the PDCCH repetition is indicated by higher layer parameter searchspaceLinkingID, the PDCCH repetition mechanism should be applied only when both SS sets are monitored in a search space set group. However, the exting description in 38.213 implies that PDCCH repetition mecahnisms are always applied even when only one of the two SS sets is monitored in a search space set group, which is not consistent with the conclusion above.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: In several sections, reference to section 10.4 is excluded in the description for PDCCH repetiton.
old_anchors.title: CR on PDCCH repetition with SSSG switching

old_anchors.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE would apply the wrong set of power control parameters to PUSCH transmission to a TRP associated to the second SRS resource set
old_anchors.properties_json: {"consequencesIfNotApproved":"UE would apply the wrong set of power control parameters to PUSCH transmission to a TRP associated to the second SRS resource set","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"344.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208067","reasonForChange":"When two SRS resource sets are configured for  DCI format 0_1 or DCI format 0_2 and if a SRS resource set indicator indicating one of the SRS resource sets  is present  in a DCI, but an corresponding SRI field is not present in the DCI, a default power control parameter is supposed to be used and if the open-loop power control parameter set indication  field  is not included in the DCI, the the default parameters are specified by the the first and second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets for the first and second SRS resource sets, respectively. \n\nHowever, in the current specification, it is stated that the first P0-PUSCH-AlphaSet in p0-AlphaSets is used as the default power control parameters  when either one of the two SRS resource sets is indicated, which is incorrect.","reservationDate":"8/25/2022 6:28:57 AM","status":"agreed","summaryOfChange":"A change is made to state that when the second SRS resource set is indicated in the DCI, parameters in the second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets are used  for PUSCH power control.","tdocNumber":"R1-2208067","title":"CR on default PUSCH power control parameters for mTRP PUSCH","tsgCRPack":"RP-222400","type":"CR","uploadedDate":"2022-08-28T18:21:16.693000"}
old_anchors.reasonForChange:
When two SRS resource sets are configured for  DCI format 0_1 or DCI format 0_2 and if a SRS resource set indicator indicating one of the SRS resource sets  is present  in a DCI, but an corresponding SRI field is not present in the DCI, a default power control parameter is supposed to be used and if the open-loop power control parameter set indication  field  is not included in the DCI, the the default parameters are specified by the the first and second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets for the first and second SRS resource sets, respectively. 

However, in the current specification, it is stated that the first P0-PUSCH-AlphaSet in p0-AlphaSets is used as the default power control parameters  when either one of the two SRS resource sets is indicated, which is incorrect.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: A change is made to state that when the second SRS resource set is indicated in the DCI, parameters in the second P0-PUSCH-AlphaSets in p0-AlphaSets are used  for PUSCH power control.
old_anchors.title: CR on default PUSCH power control parameters for mTRP PUSCH

old_anchors.consequencesIfNotApproved: The association between the two sets of power control parameters for PUSCH repetition and the two SRS resource sets is absent in 38.213.
old_anchors.properties_json: {"consequencesIfNotApproved":"The association between the two sets of power control parameters for PUSCH repetition and the two SRS resource sets is absent in 38.213.","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"345.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208068","reasonForChange":"If a UE is provided two SRS resource sets for PUSCH repetition by RRC, one or two SRI(s)/SRS resource set(s) can be indicated for PUSCH transmission via SRS resource set indicator in DCI. When the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11, two SRS resource sets are associated with different PUSCHs, and two sets of power control parameters would be determined according to 38.213. However, the association between the two sets of power control parameters and the two SRS resource sets is absent in 38.213. It is unclear whether the first and second set of power control parameters (e.g. ) are associated with the first and second set of SRS resource set, or associated with the first and second PUSCH repetition respectively. They are different cases when the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11. When the SRS resource set indicator value is 00 and 01, only one SRS resource set is associated with PUSCH and only one set of power control parameters is determined based on 38.213, and there is no ambiguity for the mapping.","reservationDate":"8/25/2022 6:28:58 AM","status":"agreed","summaryOfChange":"The first set of power control parameters is associated with the first SRS resource set, and the second set of power control parameters is associated with the second SRS resource set.","tdocNumber":"R1-2208068","title":"CR for power control of mTRP PUSCH repetition","tsgCRPack":"RP-222400","type":"CR","uploadedDate":"2022-08-28T18:21:16.693000"}
old_anchors.reasonForChange: If a UE is provided two SRS resource sets for PUSCH repetition by RRC, one or two SRI(s)/SRS resource set(s) can be indicated for PUSCH transmission via SRS resource set indicator in DCI. When the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11, two SRS resource sets are associated with different PUSCHs, and two sets of power control parameters would be determined according to 38.213. However, the association between the two sets of power control parameters and the two SRS resource sets is absent in 38.213. It is unclear whether the first and second set of power control parameters (e.g. ) are associated with the first and second set of SRS resource set, or associated with the first and second PUSCH repetition respectively. They are different cases when the SRS resource set indicator value is 10 and 11. When the SRS resource set indicator value is 00 and 01, only one SRS resource set is associated with PUSCH and only one set of power control parameters is determined based on 38.213, and there is no ambiguity for the mapping.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: The first set of power control parameters is associated with the first SRS resource set, and the second set of power control parameters is associated with the second SRS resource set.
old_anchors.title: CR for power control of mTRP PUSCH repetition

old_anchors.properties_json: {"consequencesIfNotApproved":"PUSCH repetition Type B cannot be scheduled when overlap with SSBs associated with additional PCIs.","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"311.0","crRevision":"1.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208083","reasonForChange":"In 38.214, SSBs associated with additional PCIs are not considered as invalid symbols for PUSCH repetition Type B. \nAvoiding such conflict by network implementation may not be practical since scheduling PUSCH repetition type B by any TRP may have to be delayed until after any SSB associated with any additional PCI, which is against the motivation of PUSCH repetition Type B for latency reduction.","reservationDate":"8/25/2022 7:25:21 AM","status":"agreed","summaryOfChange":"In 38.214, add SSBs indicated by ssb-PositionsInBurst in SSB-MTCAdditionalPCI as invalid symbols for PUSCH repetition Type B.","tdocNumber":"R1-2208083","title":"CR on inter-cell mTRP with PUSCH repetition TypeB","tsgCRPack":"RP-222400","type":"CR","uploadedDate":"2022-08-28T18:21:16.803000"}
old_anchors.reasonForChange:
In 38.214, SSBs associated with additional PCIs are not considered as invalid symbols for PUSCH repetition Type B. 
Avoiding such conflict by network implementation may not be practical since scheduling PUSCH repetition type B by any TRP may have to be delayed until after any SSB associated with any additional PCI, which is against the motivation of PUSCH repetition Type B for latency reduction.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: In 38.214, add SSBs indicated by ssb-PositionsInBurst in SSB-MTCAdditionalPCI as invalid symbols for PUSCH repetition Type B.
old_anchors.title: CR on inter-cell mTRP with PUSCH repetition TypeB

old_anchors.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE behavior will remain undefined when SSBs that the UE measures for L1-RSRP/SINR (and are not associated with the PCI that has active TCI states) overlap with UL channels/signals.
old_anchors.reasonForChange:
For inter-cell mTRP in FeMIMO, the following has been agreed in RAN1#108-e:


In 38.213, the “active additional PCI” in the agreement is captured as the PCI associated with the active TCI states. However, this is problematic as UE still measures SSBs (L1 measurment) from the PCIs not associated with the active TCI states.
When SSBs that the UE measures for L1-RSRP/SINR (and are not associated with the PCI that has active TCI states) overlap with UL channels/signals, there is no procedure currently defined as to whether the UE should measure the SSB or transmit the UL channel/signal given that the UE is not capable of full-duplex operation in TDD.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: Remove the condition “associated to physical cell ID with active TCI states” in relevant sections.
old_anchors.title: CR on inter-cell mTRP when SSBs of additional PCI overlap with UL

old_anchors.reasonForChange:
In RAN1#109-e, following was agreed. However, TP was not discussed, due to the lack of time. Hence, we propose TP to capture the agreement.
Agreement
If scheduling offset < threshold (timeDurationForQCL ), regardless of configuration of followUnifiedTCIstate 
If the indicated TCI is associated with PCI different from serving cell PCI  (i.e. inter-cell),
UE should apply Rel.15 default QCL assumption for both non-UE dedicated and UE dedicated PDSCH (i.e. QCL assumption of the lowest CORESET ID in the latest slot)
If the QCL -TypeD property for default beams in a slot for CCs in a band are different, the default beam for the CC with lowest ID is prioritized, i.e. the default beam for the CC with lowest ID is applied to all the CCs in a band
If the indicated TCI  is associated with serving cell PCI  (i.e. intra-cell), UE  always uses indicated TCI  for both UE -dedicated/non-UE -dedicated PDSCH  (i.e. no need to consider default QCL ) 
The same approach above is applied to default beam for aperiodic CSI -RS
Note: UE is not expected to receive a non-UE dedicated PDSCH if the source RS of the TCI state of the corresponding PDSCH is not associated with the serving cell PCID . 
Note: when the above was agreed on email, last two sub-bullets were two “bullets”, which are applied to all the agreement. However, in final chairman’s note, these two bullets are incorrectly noted as sub-bullets.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: Specify agreed default QCL assumption for unified TCI state for PDSCH in clause 5.1.5 and for A-CSI-RS in clause 5.2.1.5.1.
old_anchors.title: CR on default QCL for unified TCI state for PDSCH and A-CSI-RS

old_anchors.consequencesIfNotApproved: The specification is inconsistent with the newly introduced UE capability FG23-7-1c which can support multiple candidate values of X, rather than a fixed value.
old_anchors.properties_json:
{"consequencesIfNotApproved":"The specification is inconsistent with the newly introduced UE capability FG23-7-1c which can support multiple candidate values of X, rather than a fixed value.","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"318.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208181","reasonForChange":"In RAN1#109-e UE capability discussion, it was agreed to introduce a new basic feature for MTRP CSI, FG23-7-1c, which indicates the number of CPUs occupied by an NCJT CSI calculation which can be 2, 3 or 4. old_anchors.properties_json: {"consequencesIfNotApproved":"It is ambiguous how the UE will determine PUCCH resource or the number of CSI reports if multiplexing NCJT CSI reports, without specific assumption of rank combination or transmission hypothesis.","crCategory":"F","crNumber":"354.0","for":"Agreement","id":"tdoc:R1-2208184","reasonForChange":"For Rel-17 NCJT CSI reporting, the UE will report a joint RI index corresponding to one of four RI combinations. The assumption that each CSI report indicates rank 1 in 38.213 for CSI report multiplexing is ambiguous when determining PUCCH payload for Part 2 CSI since the joint RI index (or RI combination) can be interpreted differently, for example considering rank combination {1,2} as rank 1. \nMoreover, for NCJT “Mode 2”, the payload of part 2 CSI is varied depending on the preference of transmission hypothesis reported by the UE, i.e. single TRP CSI or NCJT CSI determined by the value of CRI. It gives rise to further ambiguity of determining hypothetical PUCCH resource assignment or a number of part 2 CSI reports if multiplexing NCJT Mode 2 CSI reports.","reservationDate":"8/25/2022 1:51:01 PM","status":"agreed","summaryOfChange":"It is clarified that for multiplexing CSI reports involving NCJT CSI measurement hypothesis, the UE shall assume rank combination of {1,1}. Also for “Mode 2” selecting the CSI among NCJT and single-TRP preferred by the UE, the UE shall assume NCJT measurement hypothesis used for determining PUCCH resource or the number of CSI reports.","tdocNumber":"R1-2208184","title":"Correction of CSI assumptions over multiplexing NCJT CSI reports in PUCCH","tsgCRPack":"RP-222400","type":"CR","uploadedDate":"2022-08-28T18:21:20.067000"}
old_anchors.reasonForChange:
For Rel-17 NCJT CSI reporting, the UE will report a joint RI index corresponding to one of four RI combinations. The assumption that each CSI report indicates rank 1 in 38.213 for CSI report multiplexing is ambiguous when determining PUCCH payload for Part 2 CSI since the joint RI index (or RI combination) can be interpreted differently, for example considering rank combination {1,2} as rank 1. 
Moreover, for NCJT “Mode 2”, the payload of part 2 CSI is varied depending on the preference of transmission hypothesis reported by the UE, i.e. single TRP CSI or NCJT CSI determined by the value of CRI. It gives rise to further ambiguity of determining hypothetical PUCCH resource assignment or a number of part 2 CSI reports if multiplexing NCJT Mode 2 CSI reports.
old_anchors.summaryOfChange: It is clarified that for multiplexing CSI reports involving NCJT CSI measurement hypothesis, the UE shall assume rank combination of {1,1}. Also for “Mode 2” selecting the CSI among NCJT and single-TRP preferred by the UE, the UE shall assume NCJT measurement hypothesis used for determining PUCCH resource or the number of CSI reports.
old_anchors.title: Correction of CSI assumptions over multiplexing NCJT CSI reports in PUCCH
